title: Your First VEX IQ Robot
description: Build a simple 4-wheel drive robot base and learn basic robot assembly. This is your introduction to VEX IQ robotics!
learning_objectives: Identify 10 basic VEX IQ structural and motion parts
Assemble a functional 4-wheel drive robot base
Test forward and backward movement with a controller
Document the build process in an engineering notebook
materials_needed: VEX IQ Clawbot Kit or equivalent

steps.title: Parts Scavenger Hunt
steps.content: Lay out all parts from your kit. Identify and sort: structural beams (different lengths), connectors (pins, standoffs), Smart Motors, wheels, and the Robot Brain. Use the parts identification guide to learn the names.

steps.title: Build the Rectangular Frame
steps.content: Connect four 2x15 beams to create a rectangular base frame using corner connectors. Make sure all connections are secure by pushing pins all the way through.

steps.title: Attach Motors and Wheels
steps.content: Mount one Smart Motor on each side of the frame. Attach wheels to the motor shafts. Ensure wheels spin freely without rubbing against the frame.

steps.title: Test Drive
steps.content: Connect the Robot Brain and motors. Pair the controller. Test driving the robot forward, backward, and turning. Adjust wheel alignment if needed.

steps.title: Document Your Build
steps.content: In your engineering notebook, draw your robot from the side and top view. Label at least 5 parts. Write 2-3 sentences about what you learned today.

title: Robot Parts Detective
description: A fun scavenger hunt activity to learn the names and functions of 15 common VEX IQ parts.
learning_objectives: Correctly identify and name 15 VEX IQ parts
Categorize parts by function (structure, motion, control)
Understand the purpose of each part type

steps.title: Introduction to Part Families
steps.content: Learn about three part families: STRUCTURE (beams, plates, connectors), MOTION (motors, wheels, gears), and CONTROL (brain, sensors, battery).

steps.title: Scavenger Hunt
steps.content: Find these parts in your kit: 2x10 beam, 2x15 beam, corner connector, standoff, Smart Motor, wheel, gear, Robot Brain, controller, battery, LED sensor, bumper switch, distance sensor, gyro sensor, cable.

steps.title: Sort and Categorize
steps.content: Place each part in the correct family bin (Structure, Motion, or Control). Discuss why each part belongs in its category.

title: Your First Robot Program
description: Write and test your first VEX IQ program to make the robot move forward, wait, and stop.
learning_objectives: Understand basic sequential programming
Write a 3-command program (forward, wait, stop)
Test and debug a simple program
Measure and adjust robot movement distance

steps.title: Open VEXcode IQ
steps.content: Launch VEXcode IQ software. Create a new project named 'First Program'. Connect your robot via USB or wirelessly.

steps.title: Build the Program
steps.content: Drag blocks into the workspace: [When started] → [Drive forward] → [Wait 2 seconds] → [Stop driving]. Set motor speed to 50%.

steps.title: Download and Test
steps.content: Download the program to your robot. Place robot on the floor. Press Start. Measure how far it travels. Did it go the expected distance?

steps.title: Adjust and Improve
steps.content: Modify the wait time to make the robot travel exactly 12 inches (30 cm). Test multiple times. Record your final wait value.

title: Understanding Team Roles
description: Learn about the four key roles in a VEX IQ team and practice rotating through each one.
learning_objectives: Identify the four team roles: Builder, Programmer, Driver, and Documenter
Experience each role through hands-on practice
Understand how roles work together
Reflect on personal strengths and preferences

steps.title: Meet the Roles
steps.content: BUILDER: Assembles and modifies the robot. PROGRAMMER: Writes code for autonomous and driver control. DRIVER: Operates the robot during matches. DOCUMENTER: Records decisions, data, and progress in the notebook.

steps.title: Role Rotation Activity
steps.content: Each team member tries each role for 3 minutes: build something small, write a simple program, drive the robot through cones, document the activity.

steps.title: Reflection and Planning
steps.content: Discuss: Which role did you enjoy most? Which was most challenging? How do the roles depend on each other? Agree on role assignments for next session.

title: Engineering Notebook Basics
description: Learn how to set up and use an engineering notebook to document your robot design journey.
learning_objectives: Create a properly formatted notebook title page
Learn the STEM notebook documentation format
Practice technical drawing with labeled diagrams
Write clear descriptions of design decisions

steps.title: Create Your Title Page
steps.content: On page 1, write: Team name and number, team members' names, season/competition, date started. Add a team logo or robot sketch.

steps.title: Learn the Entry Format
steps.content: Each entry should have: Date, Goal/Objective, Procedure (what you did), Observations (what happened), Conclusion (what you learned), Signature.

steps.title: Practice Technical Drawing
steps.content: Draw your robot or a simple mechanism from today. Use a ruler for straight lines. Add labels with arrows pointing to important parts. Include measurements.

steps.title: Write Your First Entry
steps.content: Document today's activity using the entry format. Describe what you built, programmed, or learned. Sign and date it.

title: Build a Simple Claw
description: Design and build a basic claw mechanism to pick up game elements. Learn about mechanical advantage.
learning_objectives: Design a functional claw using VEX IQ parts
Test the claw with different objects
Understand basic lever mechanics
Iterate to improve grip strength

steps.title: Plan Your Design
steps.content: Sketch a simple claw design on paper. It should have: two 'fingers' that open and close, a motor to control it, and a way to attach to the robot. Think about how wide it needs to open.

steps.title: Build the Claw Frame
steps.content: Build a base structure to mount the claw. Create two 'fingers' using beams that can pivot. Use pins as pivot points.

steps.title: Add the Motor Mechanism
steps.content: Connect the Smart Motor to control the claw opening and closing. Use gears or direct connection. Test that both fingers move together.

steps.title: Test and Improve
steps.content: Try picking up different objects: cubes, balls, light items, heavy items. What works well? What doesn't? Add rubber bands for better grip if needed.

title: Introduction to Gears
description: Explore how gears work by building simple gear trains and discovering gear ratios.
learning_objectives: Build 2-gear and 3-gear trains
Understand driver vs. driven gears
Observe speed and torque changes
Calculate simple gear ratios

steps.title: Build a 2-Gear Train
steps.content: Mount two gears next to each other so their teeth mesh. Connect a motor to the first gear. Turn it on and observe. Which direction does each gear spin?

steps.title: Test Different Sizes
steps.content: Try these combinations: 12-tooth to 36-tooth, 36-tooth to 12-tooth, 12-tooth to 60-tooth. What happens to the speed of the second gear?

steps.title: Understand Gear Ratios
steps.content: Count how many times the driver gear turns for one full turn of the driven gear. This is the gear ratio! A 12:36 ratio means 3 turns of the small gear = 1 turn of the large gear.

steps.title: Document Your Findings
steps.content: In your notebook, draw each gear train you built. Label the gear sizes. Write whether it increased speed or torque (power).

title: Drive in a Square
description: Program your robot to drive in a perfect square path. Learn about loops and turning.
learning_objectives: Create a program using sequential commands
Use turns to change robot direction
Measure and verify accurate movement
Understand the concept of loops (bonus)
materials_needed: Robot with Smart Motors and gyro sensor

steps.title: Plan the Square
steps.content: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right-angle (90°) turns. Decide how long each side should be (suggestion: 24 inches or 60 cm).

steps.title: Program One Side and Turn
steps.content: Write: [Drive forward for X seconds] → [Turn right 90 degrees] → [Stop]. Test to see if your robot drives straight and turns exactly 90°. Adjust as needed.

steps.title: Complete the Square
steps.content: Copy the forward and turn commands three more times to make all four sides. Download and test. Does it return to the start point?

steps.title: Improve with a Loop (Bonus)
steps.content: If you're comfortable, use a [Repeat 4 times] loop to make the code shorter and more efficient. Test again.

title: Sensor Exploration: Bumper Switch
description: Learn how to use a bumper switch sensor to detect obstacles and make decisions in your program.
learning_objectives: Mount and wire a bumper switch sensor
Write a program that responds to sensor input
Understand IF-THEN conditional logic
Test sensor reliability

steps.title: Mount the Sensor
steps.content: Attach the bumper switch to the front of your robot so it will be pressed when the robot hits something. Connect it to the Brain with a cable. Configure it in VEXcode.

steps.title: Test the Sensor
steps.content: Use the Brain screen or VEXcode to check sensor readings. Press the bumper - does the value change? Make sure it works reliably.

steps.title: Write an IF-THEN Program
steps.content: Program: [Drive forward] → [IF bumper pressed, THEN turn right and stop] → [ELSE keep driving]. This makes the robot avoid walls!

steps.title: Test with Obstacles
steps.content: Place obstacles in front of the robot. Test your program. Does it detect and avoid them? Adjust the response if needed.

title: Match Day Simulation
description: Practice a full competition match scenario with team roles, strategy, and scoring.
learning_objectives: Experience all phases of a competition match
Practice driver skills under time pressure
Work with a partner team (Mix & Match style)
Reflect on performance and improve

steps.title: Team Assignments and Strategy
steps.content: Divide into two-team alliances (Mix & Match style). Each alliance discusses strategy: What will each robot do in autonomous? Who scores what in driver control?

steps.title: Autonomous Period (15 seconds)
steps.content: Run your autonomous program (or simple pre-programmed movement). Score points if possible. No touching the robot allowed!

steps.title: Driver Control Period (45 seconds)
steps.content: Drivers control their robots to score game elements. Coaches can give advice but not touch robots. Keep track of points scored.

steps.title: Debrief and Improve
steps.content: Alliance meeting: What worked? What didn't? How can we improve for next match? Document 2-3 specific improvements to make.

steps.title: Practice Match 2
steps.content: Run a second match with your improvements. Did your score improve? How did teamwork change?
